Phase 3 final cleanup and retirement gate. Encapsulates owner decision A4 (defer Windows arm64 keep-vs-drop decision until after validation) and enforces the minimum one-minor-release retention window before removing any legacy generator or C binary.

2026-11-26: after the ADR revision (PR #4540) this decision covers retiring the bundled dbgen/dsdgen binaries and the legacy Python generators once benchbox-datagen is the default everywhere it has a wheel, and keep-vs-drop for Windows arm64.

Owner decisions 2026-11-26 (dialog): (1) PyPI: owner sets up Trusted Publishing once; the agent then tags and publishes 0.x releases when a stage merges and BenchBox needs it. (2) Library repo merges require the review bot (theseus review-verdict/review-gate) and essential CI, mirroring BenchBox. (3) SSB and synthetic acceptance by pre-approved objective criteria: exact row counts, zero orphan FKs, per-column null rate, distinct ratio and mean/quantiles within the legacy generator's 5-seed variation, every query returns rows on both engines where legacy did, exact DuckDB/DataFusion agreement; escalate only on failure. (4) Upstream gaps: implement in benchbox-datagen-core on upstream's public API; upstream PRs are contributions, never waited on; no vendoring. (10) Feature batches: A library TPC; B BenchBox integration; C SSB + 8 synthetic in parallel; D cutovers + re-baseline; E Parquet semantics + DuckLake convert in parallel with A; F retirement.
description:
## Problem
Keeping retired legacy generators and per-OS C dbgen/dsdgen binaries indefinitely adds maintenance burden, but deleting them prematurely would break Windows arm64 (where tpcgen-cli 4.0.0 ships no wheel), TPC-H/TPC-DS refresh paths (RF1/RF2 and -update), or reproduction of published corpus results.

## Change
- After at least one minor BenchBox release running on the validated new defaults, perform a retirement audit across every migrated benchmark:
  1. Re-check upstream tpcgen-cli wheel coverage for Windows arm64 and refresh-stream support (TPC-H RF1/RF2, TPC-DS -update).
  2. Audit whether published-result reproduction still requires --datagen-backend legacy for any Tier 1, Tier 2 (SSB v1), or Tier 3 benchmark.
  3. Obtain explicit owner sign-off on Windows arm64 policy (owner decision A4: keep bundled C binaries there vs drop native TPC datagen support on Windows arm64) and on which legacy generators/binaries to retire; record the decision in docs/internal/adr/adr-benchbox-datagen.md.
  4. Remove only confirmed-obsolete dbgen/dsdgen binaries (updating benchbox/_binaries/SHA256MANIFEST.json and benchbox/utils/datagen_version.py) and confirmed-obsolete legacy Python generator code paths, with a changelog.d/ fragment if user-facing.

## Decision gates
- Hard waiting gate: do not remove any legacy path until at least one minor release has shipped on the new defaults.
- Hard owner decision gate: explicit owner approval required for Windows arm64 keep-vs-drop (A4) and before deleting any binary or legacy generator needed to reproduce published results.

## Guardrails
- NEVER remove qgen, dsqgen, tpcds.idx, or TPC query templates from benchbox/_binaries/.
- NEVER delete dsdgen (or dbgen) while TPC-DS or TPC-H refresh paths still require it.
- NEVER delete a platform binary without confirmed wheel coverage or explicit owner authorization to drop that platform.
- Follow AGENTS.md ([CHANGELOG-001], [COMMENT-POLICY-001], linked worktree, make pr-preflight, merged PR).
